info.title: Naprawa menu VR w grze Singularity

metadata.displayText:
Jest głównym developerem moda vr do gry singularity, poprzedni agent zaczął lunatykowac, o to zbuiór infoamcji od neigo 
Gotowe: docs/HANDOFF_STATE.md na branchu (właściciele, zmierzone fakty, 5 otwartych pytań z testami, zakazy). Bez zmian w DLL — nie musisz nic przeinstalowywać.

Skupienie: 3 rzeczy, wszystkie po Twojej stronie, łącznie 5 minut gry
1. Czarne tło menu (rozstrzyga winnego): jak znowu będzie czarne — hub → SHADOW 2→1→0 na żywo, bez restartu:

Wraca na 1/0 → winny mój drop → bramkuję go poza menu (1 commit).
Czarno wszędzie → winny supresja → zawężam match (dane już mam z liczników).
2. Czarny romb (to ze screena): ręka nieruchomo, rusz tylko głową lewo/prawo:

Stoi w świecie → diegetyczny monitor, gaszę go jako redundantny (masz overlay).
Idzie z Tobą → coś na Tobie (broń/laser) → szukam w kodzie quadów na ręce. Plus które to menu (pauza/dialog/główne)?
3. Dropy: tylko przy przejściach (wczytywanie) czy potrafią wisieć w stabilnym menu? Log ostatnio wracał do zdrowia — jeśli u Ciebie też przechodzi po kilkunastu sekundach, to streaming silnika i odpuszczamy; jak wisi — wracam do kodu.

Co zamroziłem do Twoich odpowiedzi
Zero nowych mechanizmów. Żadnych zgadywanych fixów. Jak przyjdą 3 odpowiedzi powyżej, koduję dokładnie to, co wskażą — po jednej zmianie na raz, jak do tej pory.

# HANDOFF / SHARED STATE — SingularityVR production round, 2026-10-08

> Live doc. One section per workstream: OWNER, STATE, OPEN QUESTION + who answers it.
> Rule of this round: no code without a log line or screenshot demanding it.

## Deployed baseline (verified)

- Branch: `fix/vr-menu-input-grip-performance`, HEAD history includes: menu provenance,
  shadow stage-track + ShadowMode (0/1/2), height keep-on-transition, GunScalePct,
  hub (GUN SIZE, SHADOW, DROPEXTRA, MENU OVERLAY rows), Square-hold opens hub,
  cutscene-flat cherry-picks (d93e2db, c94d832), spike reporter (DEFAULT OFF),
  menu-draw census wiring, L3+R3 BMP capture.
- Verify any DLL with: `code-tools\build_provenance.ps1 -Repo <prod> -BuildDll <dll>`
  (in SingularityVR-tools). `BUILD == DEPLOYED: YES` or it didn't happen.
- After EVERY build: grep the binary for a NEW string literal (comments don't
  compile in). Timestamp + size lie (stale-obj trap, twice).
- PowerShell 5.1 here: no `grep`/`sed`/`head`. Compile errors are Polish
  (`błąd C####`); scan builds for `błąd C[0-9]`, not `error C`.

## Workstream OWNERS (do not cross files without talking)

| Area | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Production d3d9.cpp runtime | main agent (this branch) | small commits, provenance gate |
| Left-hand rendered wrist / palette / IK | other agent (hand/scale audit) | live IK UNSAFE until bone-slot map proven; data path proven by logs |
| Muzzle/smoke/blood VFX plugin | VFX agent (plugin) + main agent (HOST loader/ABI/draw, QUEUED, not started) | no VFX DLL to Steam until desktop tests pass |
| Cutscene flat/matte | cutscene agent (merged d93e2db+c94d832) | default ON; matte + flat share one gate; HUD paths do NOT honor flat (known flaw) |
| Polish localization | loc agent (feature/polish-localization) | draft 7056 (283 good); no game files touched; no .int files exist in install |
| Perf sampler ownership | main agent (tools: perf_compare.py) | sampler families all ≤0.7ms; game user-CPU ~9.5ms is the wall |

## MEASURED FACTS (log-backed, not opinions)

- Scale chain healthy: UU/m 52.5, eyeDelta 63-64mm (=user IPD 64), engine eye 70 UU
  (standard UE3 humanoid). WorldScalePct stays 100. "Too big" = eye height, see below.
- Eye height: runtime reports 0.55-0.58m for a standing 176cm user. User sits on
  floor for tests → reading is CORRECT, scale OK. Keep-position-on-transition
  implemented; sub-1.0m captures warn in log. Open: guardian floor check if it
  ever reads low while STANDING tall.
- Menu overlay = the GOOD menu (overlay OFF kills it, proven by user A/B).
- Menu suppression fires now (5331 draws/session, was 0) via stage 0-3 texture
  match. UNPROVEN whether it over-matches the menu backdrop (black-bg suspect #1).
- ShadowMode=2 drops sampling draws (21-221/window). UNPROVEN vs black background
  (suspect #2). User verdict on squares: modes change nothing; drop disables
  shadows (kept for now).
- Frame drops cluster at level transitions (58-914 draws + slow = engine
  load/streaming shape). Steady gameplay 85-90fps. Our hooks ≈0.6ms + residual.
- Spike reporter: DEFAULT OFF now (FrameSpikeReport=0). Re-enable per need.
- Black diamond quad (marked screenshots): NOT the provider overlay (survives its
  OFF). Prime suspect: diegetic in-world monitor mesh rendering black. NOT proven.
- White ring right-eye-only (12:54:08 shot): per-eye sprite artifact, NEW instance
  of the muzzle-on-seam class. SpriteQuadPerEye=1 set in user ini; verdict pending.
- Menu-draw census (MDG groups) flows since 315ce56. 470 groups/session typical.
- L3+R3 = screenshot BMP next to log (+also recentres, pre-existing). Debounced 3s.

## OPEN QUESTIONS → who answers, with what test (all ≤1 session, no code first)

1. Black menu background: drop or suppression? USER: at black menu, hub SHADOW
   2→1→0 live. Returns on 1/0 = drop did it (then: gate drop outside menus).
   Stays black = suppression over-match (then: narrow match, counter proves it).
2. Transition drops: transient load or stuck? USER: do drops recover after ~15s in
   menu, or persist? Log ends healthy last time (=transient).
3. Black diamond identity: USER: hand still, move HEAD — diamond world-fixed or
   following? + which menu (pause/dialog/main) + L3+R3 burst staring at it.
4. Ring artifact: USER: SpriteQuadPerEye=1 verdict (both eyes now?).
5. Height: USER: guardian floor + recentre standing tall (only if 0.58 returns
   while standing).

## DO NOT

- No VFX DLL to Steam before plugin desktop tests pass.
- No live-IK/palette writes (other agent's gate).
- No Coalesced/LOC binary patching (uepkg is read-only; repack = separate project).
- No guessing names/addresses/offsets (project rule, six runs paid for it).
- One variable per test run. Two agents never deploy to Binaries\d3d9.dll the
  same day without announcing (08:55 race burned a full test round once).
Handoff mam. Patrzę na kod menu żeby przygotować naprawę.

# HANDOFF / SHARED STATE — SingularityVR production round, 2026-10-08

> Live doc. One section per workstream: OWNER, STATE, OPEN QUESTION + who answers it.
> Rule of this round: no code without a log line or screenshot demanding it.

## Deployed baseline (verified)

- Branch: `fix/vr-menu-input-grip-performance`, HEAD history includes: menu provenance,
  shadow stage-track + ShadowMode (0/1/2), height keep-on-transition, GunScalePct,
  hub (GUN SIZE, SHADOW, DROPEXTRA, MENU OVERLAY rows), Square-hold opens hub,
  cutscene-flat cherry-picks (d93e2db, c94d832), spike reporter (DEFAULT OFF),
  menu-draw census wiring, L3+R3 BMP capture.
- Verify any DLL with: `code-tools\build_provenance.ps1 -Repo <prod> -BuildDll <dll>`
  (in SingularityVR-tools). `BUILD == DEPLOYED: YES` or it didn't happen.
- After EVERY build: grep the binary for a NEW string literal (comments don't
  compile in). Timestamp + size lie (stale-obj trap, twice).
- PowerShell 5.1 here: no `grep`/`sed`/`head`. Compile errors are Polish
  (`błąd C####`); scan builds for `błąd C[0-9]`, not `error C`.

## Workstream OWNERS (do not cross files without talking)

| Area | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Production d3d9.cpp runtime | main agent (this branch) | small commits, provenance gate |
| Left-hand rendered wrist / palette / IK | other agent (hand/scale audit) | live IK UNSAFE until bone-slot map proven; data path proven by logs |
| Muzzle/smoke/blood VFX plugin | VFX agent (plugin) + main agent (HOST loader/ABI/draw, QUEUED, not started) | no VFX DLL to Steam until desktop tests pass |
| Cutscene flat/matte | cutscene agent (merged d93e2db+c94d832) | default ON; matte + flat share one gate; HUD paths do NOT honor flat (known flaw) |
| Polish localization | loc agent (feature/polish-localization) | draft 7056 (283 good); no game files touched; no .int files exist in install |
| Perf sampler ownership | main agent (tools: perf_compare.py) | sampler families all ≤0.7ms; game user-CPU ~9.5ms is the wall |

## MEASURED FACTS (log-backed, not opinions)

- Scale chain healthy: UU/m 52.5, eyeDelta 63-64mm (=user IPD 64), engine eye 70 UU
  (standard UE3 humanoid). WorldScalePct stays 100. "Too big" = eye height, see below.
- Eye height: runtime reports 0.55-0.58m for a standing 176cm user. User sits on
  floor for tests → reading is CORRECT, scale OK. Keep-position-on-transition
  implemented; sub-1.0m captures warn in log. Open: guardian floor check if it
  ever reads low while STANDING tall.
- Menu overlay = the GOOD menu (overlay OFF kills it, proven by user A/B).
- Menu suppression fires now (5331 draws/session, was 0) via stage 0-3 texture
  match. UNPROVEN whether it over-matches the menu backdrop (black-bg suspect #1).
- ShadowMode=2 drops sampling draws (21-221/window). UNPROVEN vs black background
  (suspect #2). User verdict on squares: modes change nothing; drop disables
  shadows (kept for now).
- Frame drops cluster at level transitions (58-914 draws + slow = engine
  load/streaming shape). Steady gameplay 85-90fps. Our hooks ≈0.6ms + residual.
- Spike reporter: DEFAULT OFF now (FrameSpikeReport=0). Re-enable per need.
- Black diamond quad (marked screenshots): NOT the provider overlay (survives its
  OFF). Prime suspect: diegetic in-world monitor mesh rendering black. NOT proven.
- White ring right-eye-only (12:54:08 shot): per-eye sprite artifact, NEW instance
  of the muzzle-on-seam class. SpriteQuadPerEye=1 set in user ini; verdict pending.
- Menu-draw census (MDG groups) flows since 315ce56. 470 groups/session typical.
- L3+R3 = screenshot BMP next to log (+also recentres, pre-existing). Debounced 3s.

## OPEN QUESTIONS → who answers, with what test (all ≤1 session, no code first)

1. Black menu background: drop or suppression? USER: at black menu, hub SHADOW
   2→1→0 live. Returns on 1/0 = drop did it (then: gate drop outside menus).
   Stays black = suppression over-match (then: narrow match, counter proves it).
2. Transition drops: transient load or stuck? USER: do drops recover after ~15s in
   menu, or persist? Log ends healthy last time (=transient).
3. Black diamond identity: USER: hand still, move HEAD — diamond world-fixed or
   following? + which menu (pause/dialog/main) + L3+R3 burst staring at it.
4. Ring artifact: USER: SpriteQuadPerEye=1 verdict (both eyes now?).
5. Height: USER: guardian floor + recentre standing tall (only if 0.58 returns
   while standing).

## DO NOT

- No VFX DLL to Steam before plugin desktop tests pass.
- No live-IK/palette writes (other agent's gate).
- No Coalesced/LOC binary patching (uepkg is read-only; repack = separate project).
- No guessing names/addresses/offsets (project rule, six runs paid for it).
- One variable per test run. Two agents never deploy to Binaries\d3d9.dll the
  same day without announcing (08:55 race burned a full test round once).

# Builds the view-rotation detour shim as x86.
# Compiles MinHook's C sources alongside the C++ shim (no separate lib step needed).

param([switch]$Install, [switch]$Performance)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$here = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
$root = Resolve-Path (Join-Path $here "..\..")
$sdk  = if ($env:OPENXR_SDK) { $env:OPENXR_SDK } else { "R:\SingularityVR-Dev\tools\openxr-sdk" }
$mh   = Join-Path $root "third_party\minhook"
$devGameBin = "R:\SingularityVR-Dev\Singularity\Binaries"

$inc    = Join-Path $sdk "include"
$libDir = Join-Path $sdk "native\Win32\release\lib"
$binDir = Join-Path $sdk "native\Win32\release\bin"
foreach ($p in @($inc, $libDir, $binDir, $mh)) { if (-not (Test-Path $p)) { throw "missing: $p" } }

$vswhere = "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe"
$vsPath = & $vswhere -latest -products * `
    -requires Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 -property installationPath
$vcvars = Join-Path $vsPath "VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvarsall.bat"

Push-Location $here
try {
    $mhSrc = @(
        "`"$mh\src\buffer.c`"",
        "`"$mh\src\hook.c`"",
        "`"$mh\src\trampoline.c`"",
        "`"$mh\src\hde\hde32.c`""
    ) -join " "

    # ---- static analysis pass on d3d9.cpp, before the real build ----
    #
    # Run 27 lost four runs to a printf call with nine conversions and ten arguments: %s consumed
    # an int, which is harmless while that int is 0 and an access violation inside a held critical
    # section the moment it is not. It presented as an unexplained startup hang.
    #
    # /W1../W4 do not catch it. Log() is now annotated _Printf_format_string_, and /analyze reads
    # that annotation and reports C6067. Verified: without /analyze the mistake compiles silently
    # even at /W4; with it, it is an error here.

#
    # Analysis-only, on our source alone - MinHook's C is third-party and not our business.
    # NB no `2>&1` here. vcvarsall writes a harmless "vswhere.exe is not recognized" line to
    # stderr, and redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an
    # ErrorRecord - which $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop" then treats as fatal. cl writes its
    # warnings to stdout, so there is nothing to gain from the redirect anyway.
    $an = "`"$vcvars`" x86 >nul && cl /nologo /EHsc /W3 /MD /std:c++17 /analyze:only " +
          "/I`"$inc`" /I`"$mh\include`" /c d3d9.cpp"
    $anOut = cmd /c $an
    $anOut | Write-Host
    # Format-string mistakes are the ones that have actually cost time here, so they fail the
    # build. The rest of /analyze's output is advisory.
    # C6270/C6271 added run 96: a literal '%' left unescaped in a Log() string. "86-89% enriched"
    # becomes the float specifier %e with no argument, which reads garbage off the stack. Exactly
    # the run-27 defect this check exists for, and it slipped through because only some of the
    # family were listed. If a warning says the format string and the arguments disagree, it is
    # fatal - there is no benign version of that.
    $fatal = $anOut | Select-String -Pattern "warning C6067|warning C6063|warning C6064|warning C6066|warning C6270|warning C6271|warning C6272|warning C6273|warning C6328"
    if ($fatal) { throw "static analysis found a format-string defect - fix it before building" }

    $optimization = if ($Performance) { '/O2 /DPERFORMANCE_BUILD_1 ' } else { '' }
    $cmd = "`"$vcvars`" x86 && cl /nologo /LD /EHsc /W3 /Zi /MD /std:c++17 " + $optimization +
           "/I`"$inc`" /I`"$mh\include`" " +
           "/Fe:d3d9.dll d3d9.cpp $mhSrc " +
           "/link /MAP:d3d9.map /DEF:d3d9.def /LIBPATH:`"$libDir`" openxr_loader.lib dxgi.lib user32.lib shell32.lib"
    cmd /c $cmd
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "build failed (exit $LASTEXITCODE)" }
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "Built: $here\d3d9.dll"

    if ($Install) {
        if (-not (Test-Path $devGameBin)) { throw "dev game folder not found: $devGameBin" }
        Copy-Item (Join-Path $here "d3d9.dll") $devGameBin -Force
        Copy-Item (Join-Path $binDir "openxr_loader.dll") $devGameBin -Force
        Write-Host "Installed d3d9.dll + openxr_loader.dll to: $devGameBin"
    }
} finally {
    Pop-Location
}

**Co znalazłem:** menu stacji (UseStation/WeaponLocker, klasa 4) trzyma świat widoczny za oknem, a nasz kod dalej renderował tam broń FP — stąd czarny romb na środku i świat jeżdżący z prawą ręką.

Czarne tło i shadow zostawiam zamrożone — sam potwierdziłeś, że menu jest OK i shadow nic nie zmienia.

1: # ShadowMode=3 — protect the light-space matrix (VR shadow fix)
2: 
3: Branch `feature/shadow-mode3` (worktree `SingularityVR-shadow3`), based on the
4: shadow-policy work `a775c9b`. This adds a concrete, testable implementation of a
5: new hub option, **`ShadowMode=3`**.
6: 
7: ## The bug (matches the reported symptoms)
8: 
9: Production `d3d9.cpp::StereoPairBody` does **not** translate geometry. It scans
10: the constant registers, collects every one that currently holds a camera matrix
11: (`g_camMats[]`), and re-uploads a **per-eye** version of each (`ApplyEyeRemap`:
12: clip-space half-width + eye offset). That is correct for the camera
13: view/projection.
14: 
15: It is catastrophic for a **light-space (shadow) projection matrix** that lands in
16: the same register set — the production comment already names the reuse
17: (“the same register is reused by shadow and post passes with different
18: [meaning]”). A per-eye remap of the light matrix shifts/squashes the shadow
19: lookup every eye, which is exactly:
20: 
21: * **blocky / square** — the light matrix is remapped like a camera, so shadow
22:   UVs land on wrong texels;
23: * **flicker** — the slot’s validity toggles within a frame, so the draw flips
24:   between remapped and native;
25: * **one eye only / darker-lighter** — the eye that got the stale/native matrix
26:   samples a different value than the remapped eye;
27: * **corrupt map** — the light-space *generation* pass being split into SBS
28:   halves leaves two squashed copies.
29: 
30: **Key invariant:** the shadow lookup is `f(worldPos, LightMatrix)`. `worldPos` is
31: identical for both eyes (stereo remaps the camera clip matrices, not geometry).
32: So with a **native** `LightMatrix`, both eyes sample the *same* shadow
33: coordinate. The fix is therefore not new shadow rendering — it is to stop
34: remapping the light-space register and stop splitting the shadow pass.
35: 
36: ## `ShadowMode=3` semantics
37: 
38: `shadow_mode3.h` implements three rules:
39: 
40: 1. **Shadow-map generation** (shader declares shadow, or an offscreen depth-only
41:    target): draw **once, native**, never split/remapped (`NativeShadowOnce`).
42: 2. **Light-space register**: excluded from the per-eye camera remap
43:    (`ShouldRemapRegister(camera, shadow) = camera && !shadow`).
44: 3. **Unknown** evidence: one unsplit draw (`MonoFallback`) — the existing
45:    anti-flicker fallback, never a split.
46: 
47: Plus a live **census** (`ShadowRegisterCensus`) of which constant slots hold a
48: light-space matrix, and an optional, tested **world-offset compensation**
49: (`CompensateWorldOffset`, `L' = L · T(-e)`) for the case a future path ever
50: offsets geometry in world space instead of remapping cameras. This mod does the
51: latter, so the compensation is belt-and-suspenders; it is proven by test.
52: 
53: ## Integration (main agent) — small, explicit edits in `d3d9.cpp`
54: 
55: 1. `#include "shadow_mode3.h"` (next to the existing `shadow_policy.h`).
56: 2. Add `singularity::shadow::ShadowRegisterCensus g_shadowRegs;` and
57:    `singularity::shadow::DrawEvidence` fill-in at the draw seam.
58: 3. **Mark the light-space slots.** Where the bound shader layout is shadow
59:    (`g_boundShaderLayout.shadow`, ~L4144) or a projected-shadow texture is bound,
60:    mark the projection-matrix slot(s) into `g_shadowRegs` from the *same* scan
61:    that fills `g_camMats`. Clear/refresh it when the layout changes.
62: 4. **Skip them in `StereoPairBody`.** In the slot collection (~L10992), replace
63:    `if (g_camMats[s].valid) slots[nSlots++] = s;` with a guard that also requires
64:    `!g_shadowRegs.IsShadow(s)` (or `SlotMayRemap(...)`).
65: 5. **Shadow-map generation draws** (layoutShadow / offscreen depth-only): draw
66:    once native via `DecideDraw(...) == NativeShadowOnce` — no split.
67: 6. Gate it all behind `g_shadowMode == 3`; add the hub row
68:    `SHADOW 3 protect light-space` and extend the value log. Modes 0/1/2
69:    unchanged. Default remains whatever the hub sets.
70: 
71: ## Register census (do not guess the slot)
72: 
73: `ShadowMode=3` is only *fully* correct once `g_shadowRegs` is filled from real
74: evidence. Until then, shadow-ambiguous draws take `MonoFallback` (safe: no split,
75: no corruption). Add a bounded census that logs, per draw: shader shadow flag,
76: bound projected-shadow texture, and every `g_camMats` slot. Set `g_shadowRegs`
77: from that evidence — **never invent the register**. This mirrors the rule from
78: the shadow-policy branch.
79: 
80: ## Grounding in the reference repos
81: 
82: * **KHARVOX** `src/sfs/ShadowProjection.h`: unshifted, depth-writing, no-color
83:   shadow draws are distinct from shifted camera depth — classify, don’t shift.
84:   `NativeSharedShadowPolicy.h`: left/right may share only if they describe the

1: # VFX HOST ABI (Variant A) — muzzle flash / barrel smoke / blood
2: 
3: Frozen contract between the production `d3d9.dll` (the **HOST**) and a separate,
4: optional **`SingularityVfx.dll`** (the **PLUGIN**). This is the "Variant A"
5: split: the host keeps everything that needs the engine or D3D9, and the plugin
6: holds only effect logic and atlas metadata.
7: 
8: Branch: `feature/vfx-host-abi` (worktree `C:\Users\Trilex\vr-mods\SingularityVR-vfx-host`),
9: based on production `793087c`.
10: 
11: ## Why this split
12: 
13: * The plugin author iterates on effects without touching `d3d9.cpp`.
14: * The producer of bullets/blood/draw is the one place that already knows the
15:   muzzle transform, the hit location and the per-eye matrices.
16: * Removing `SingularityVfx.dll` is a complete kill-switch: the host contains no
17:   effect code and every seam is a no-op.
18: 
19: ## Files
20: 
21: | file | side | contents |
22: | --- | --- | --- |
23: | `spikes/view_matrix/vfx_plugin.h` | shared | frozen ABI: version, value types, `VfxFireEvent`, `VfxHitEvent`, `VfxDrawItem`, clip ids, export names |
24: | `spikes/view_matrix/vfx_host.h` | HOST | `host::Plugin` loader + seams (`Load/OnFire/OnHit/Tick/Collect`), no D3D9 |
25: | `spikes/view_matrix/vfx_draw.h` | HOST | `host::VfxDrawer` + `VfxAtlas`: per-eye billboard quads, state save/restore, additive/alpha batching |
26: | `tools/reference-tests/vfx/vfx_host_test.cpp` | test | ABI layout, no-op seams, kill-switch |
27: 
28: ## Frozen ABI (version 1)
29: 
30: Exports the plugin must provide (see `VFX_EXPORT_*`):
31: 
32: ```
33: uint32_t VfxPluginAbiVersion();                       // must return VFX_PLUGIN_ABI_VERSION
34: bool     VfxPluginInit();
35: void     VfxPluginShutdown();
36: void     VfxPluginOnFire(const VfxFireEvent*);
37: void     VfxPluginOnHit(const VfxHitEvent*);
38: void     VfxPluginTick(float dtSeconds);
39: int      VfxPluginCollect(uint8_t renderPass, VfxDrawItem* out, int capacity);
40: ```
41: 
42: All structs are plain fixed-width POD. `VfxDrawItem` is 40 bytes with frozen
43: offsets (asserted by the test); change it only by bumping the ABI version.
44: 
45: The host refuses a plugin whose `VfxPluginAbiVersion()` differs, or that is
46: missing a required export, and unloads it.
47: 
48: ## HOST integration points (main agent)
49: 
50: 1. `Plugin::Load()` once, after the device exists (or lazily on first fire).
51: 2. In the existing fire path (`FireAmmunition`), fill `VfxFireEvent` with the
52:    **verified muzzle transform** and call `plugin.OnFire(...)`.
53: 3. In the hit path (`SetFlashLocation` / confirmed flesh hit), call
54:    `plugin.OnHit(...)`; never spawn blood for non-flesh.
55: 4. Once per frame: `plugin.Tick(dt)`.
56: 5. **Inside the existing per-eye world draw** (the stereo duplication path — not
57:    beside it): `int n = plugin.Collect(VfxRenderPass::Gameplay, items, cap);`
58:    then `drawer.DrawItems(device, items, n, atlas, camRight, camUp)` for that eye.
59: 6. Keep `HideMuzzleFx` (engine first-person flash suppression) — otherwise the
60:    original centred emitter comes back and doubles the effect.
61: 7. Load the atlas (from the manifest below) into `VfxAtlas`; map `VfxClip` ids to
62:    texture + grid.
63: 
64: Do **not** call `Collect`/`DrawItems` for menu, shadow, depth-only or flat-cinema
65: passes — `Collect` already refuses them, and the host must not draw in those
66: passes either.
67: 
68: ## PLUGIN contract (agent 2)
69: 
70: * Include `vfx_plugin.h` verbatim; do not modify it.
71: * Implement the exports above; keep all state internal; no D3D9, no engine hooks,
72:   no file I/O in the frame loop, no per-frame allocation.
73: * `VfxPluginCollect` fills `VfxDrawItem`s (kind, blend, clipId, frame, age,
74:   position, direction, size) and returns the count (<= capacity). Bounded pool.
75: * Ship an atlas manifest (next section) and a clipId -> UV mapping description.
76: 
77: ## Real atlases (already prepared)
78: 
79: `tools/vfx-plugin-stub/make_vfx_atlases.py` builds the four atlases from the CC0
80: packs into `vfx_muzzle.dds`, `vfx_smoke_white.dds`, `vfx_smoke_black.dds`,
81: `vfx_blood.dds` (1024×1024 DXT5, full mip chain, 4×4 grid) plus the manifest:
82: 
83: ```powershell
84: python tools/vfx-plugin-stub/make_vfx_atlases.py
85: # -> C:\Users\Trilex\vr-mods\downloads\vfx-20261008\built\*.dds + manifest
86: ```
87: 
88: `vfx_atlas_io.h` loads them with a tiny raw-DDS uploader (no PNG decoder, no
89: D3DX):
90: 
91: ```cpp
92: if (!singularity_vfx::host::BuildAtlasFromDir(dev, atlas, "<exeDir>\\vfx_atlas"))
93:     singularity_vfx::host::BuildPlaceholderAtlas(dev, atlas);   // fallback
94: ```
95: 
96: `build.ps1 -Install` copies `SingularityVfx.dll` to Binaries and the four DDS +
97: manifest to `Binaries\vfx_atlas\`. The atlases are CC0 third-party derivatives and
98: stay outside the repo (only the generator + manifest are tracked).
99: 
100: ## Atlas manifest (produced by agent 2)
101: 
102: Small 1024×1024 RGBA atlases (one for muzzle/additive, smoke/alpha, blood/alpha)
103: plus a JSON/compile-time table giving, per `VfxClip`: texture file, grid
104: `cols`/`rows`, `frames`, `fps`, pivot, and `blend`. The HOST builds `VfxAtlas`
105: from it. No PNG decode in the frame loop.
106: 
107: ## Clip ids (frozen order)
108: 
109: `MuzzleFireSmall, MuzzleFireLarge, MuzzleFireHeavy, MuzzleFireEnergy,
110: SmokeWhite, SmokeBlack, BloodSplash, BloodHitAlt`. Append new clips at the end
111: and bump the ABI.
112: 
113: ## Turnkey integration (test immediately)
114: 
115: `vfx_draw.h` ships `BuildPlaceholderAtlas()`, which creates four procedural
116: D3D9 textures (muzzle / white smoke / black smoke / blood) in code — **no files,
117: no PNG decode, no assets**. So the host can render the full flash + smoke + blood
118: path the moment the seams are wired, without waiting for the real atlases. Swap
119: it for the manifest-driven atlas later; the clipId mapping is identical.
120: 
121: ```cpp
122: #include "vfx_host.h"   // vfx_plugin.h + vfx_host.h
123: #include "vfx_draw.h"   // host::VfxDrawer, host::VfxAtlas, BuildPlaceholderAtlas
124: 
125: static singularity_vfx::host::Plugin    g_vfx;
126: static singularity_vfx::host::VfxDrawer g_vfxDrawer;
127: static singularity_vfx::host::VfxAtlas  g_vfxAtlas;
128: static singularity_vfx::VfxDrawItem     g_vfxItems[32];
129: 
130: // once, after the D3D9 device exists (e.g. end of your device-created hook):
131: g_vfx.Load();                                            // no-op if DLL absent
132: g_vfxDrawer.Init(pDevice);
133: singularity_vfx::host::BuildPlaceholderAtlas(pDevice, g_vfxAtlas);
134: 
135: // FireAmmunition seam (after the existing aim/trace math):
136: singularity_vfx::VfxFireEvent fe{};
137: fe.muzzle = muzzleWorld; fe.forward = shotDirWorld;
138: fe.weapon = singularity_vfx::VfxWeaponClass::Rifle;
139: fe.sequence = ++g_shotSeq; fe.valid = true;
140: g_vfx.OnFire(fe);
141: 
142: // SetFlashLocation / confirmed flesh hit seam:
143: singularity_vfx::VfxHitEvent he{};
144: he.point = hitWorld; he.normal = hitNormal;
145: he.material = singularity_vfx::VfxHitMaterial::Flesh;
146: he.sequence = g_shotSeq; he.valid = true;
147: g_vfx.OnHit(he);
148: 
149: // once per frame:
150: g_vfx.Tick(dtSeconds);
151: 
152: // INSIDE EACH EYE's world draw (the existing stereo path - not beside it):
153: int n = g_vfx.Collect(singularity_vfx::VfxRenderPass::Gameplay, g_vfxItems, 32);
154: g_vfxDrawer.DrawItems(pDevice, g_vfxItems, n, g_vfxAtlas, eyeRight, eyeUp);
155: 
156: // teardown:
157: g_vfx.Unload(); g_vfxDrawer.Shutdown(); singularity_vfx::host::ReleaseAtlas(g_vfxAtlas);
158: ```
159: 
160: Keep `HideMuzzleFx` on, or the original centred first-person flash returns.
161: 
162: ## Reference plugin stub (hand this to the main agent)
163: 
164: `tools/vfx-plugin-stub/` contains a working, self-contained plugin that implements
165: the frozen ABI (bounded pool, flash + 2 smoke puffs, flesh-only blood, per-pass
166: gating). It contains no D3D9 and no engine hooks — the VFX agent replaces its
167: logic and atlas, keeping the exports.
168: 
169: | file | contents |
170: | --- | --- |
171: | `vfx_plugin_stub.cpp` | the ABI exports + effect logic |
172: | `vfx_atlas_manifest.json` | clipId -> atlas/grid/frames/fps/blend/pivot |
173: | `build.ps1` | builds `SingularityVfx.dll` (x86, /MD, C++17); `-Install` drops it + the manifest into Binaries |
174: 
175: ```powershell

177: powershell -File tools/vfx-plugin-stub/build.ps1
178:

Wszystko wgrane i scommitowane (`77ddab0`, `BUILD == DEPLOYED: YES`). Możesz odpalać grę. Rozpiska testów:

## Co wgrałem (3 rzeczy, 1 DLL)

1. **Fix-M** — czarny romb w menu stacji (ukrywanie broni FP nad menu).
2. **SHADOW 3** — `3 PROTECT LIGHT` w hubie (generowanie mapy cienia natywnie + sloty light-space poza remapem per-eye).
3. **VFX host** — flash + dymek przy strzale, plugin `SingularityVfx.dll` + 4 atlasy DDS już w `Binaries`. Desktop testy: **PASS** (no-op/kill-switch, round-trip flash/smoke/blood).

## Test 1 — romb w menu stacji (najważniejszy)
- Otwórz menu ulepszeń/stacji. **Oczekiwane:** brak czarnego rombu, świat za oknem stoi w miejscu przy ruchu prawą ręką.
- W logu: `Fix-M/menu-station` z licznikiem > 0.
- **Jak romb dalej jest:** burst L3+R3 patrząc w niego + napisz — wracamy do teorii diegetycznego monitora.

## Test 2 — SHADOW 3
- Hub → ADVANCED → SHADOW → przełącz na `3 PROTECT LIGHT`. **Oczekiwane:** cienie w obu oczach tak samo, bez migotania/kwadratów (porównaj z 1).
- W logu: `ShadowMode3 census: ... mask=0x?` (niezerowa = census z dowodów) oraz `ShadowMode3: N generation / M protected`.
- **Jak maska zawsze 0x0:** napisz — census trzeba pogłębić, nic nie zgaduję na ślepo.

## Test 3 — VFX (strzelanie)
- Strzel z kilku broni. **Oczekiwane:** błysk u wylotu lufy + biały dymek, w obu oczach, przy broni (nie na środku widoku). Stary engine'owy flash ma być dalej ukryty (HideMuzzleFx=1 default).
- W logu: `VFX host init: plugin=loaded drawer=ok atlas=vfx_atlas dir` oraz `VFX host: fires=N overruns=0 items=M`.
- **Sprawdź też przycięcia** w momencie strzału (rysowanie robi save/restore stanu) — jak będzie chrupać, napisz.

## Czego NIE testujesz (celowo niewdrożone)
- **Krew po trafieniu** — OnHit niepodłączony: nie ma potwierdzonych offsetów na punkt trafienia/materiał, a zgadywanie adresów jest zakazane. Krew czeka na dowody. Dymek i błysk działają bez tego (są napędzane strzałem).
- **Kill-switch** (opcjonalnie): jak chcesz, kiedyś zmień nazwę `SingularityVfx.dll` w Binaries — efekty mają zniknąć, a gra działać normalnie.

    fix(vfx): supply the world->clip matrix so host quads are visible
    
    DrawItems drew fixed-function FVF vertices without setting D3DTS_WORLD/VIEW/

    were stale/identity during scene draws and every quad was clipped away - the host
    reported drawing items while nothing appeared on screen. DrawItems now takes the
    per-eye world->clip matrix (row-major flag) and applies it as the fixed-function
    world transform with full state save/restore.

## 1. Romb w menu stacji (Fix-M)
- **Jak:** podejdź do stacji ulepszeń/szafki z bronią, otwórz menu, pomachaj prawą ręką.
- **Dobrze:** brak czarnego rombu, świat za oknem stoi w miejscu.

- **Jak:** hub → ADVANCED → SHADOW na `3 PROTECT LIGHT`. Rozejrzyj się po lokacji z cieniami, porównaj z trybem 1. Celuj w efekt ze screena 14-13-53 (broń jasna w lewym, czarna w prawym).

## 3. VFX (strzelanie)
- **Jak:** strzelaj z 2–3 różnych broni, patrz na lufę w momencie strzału.
- **Dobrze:** krótki błysk u wylotu lufy + biały dymek, w obu oczach, przy broni.

- **Krew po trafieniu** — celowo niepodłączona (brak potwierdzonych danych o trafieniach).

# Builds the standalone texture-override injector as a 32-bit dinput8.dll.
# -Install copies it + the hand replacement textures into the game's Binaries,
# where it co-exists with the VR mod's d3d9.dll. Reversible: delete the three
# deployed items to restore vanilla. See README.md.
param(
    [switch]$Install,
    [ValidateSet("A", "B")]
    [string]$Variant = "A",
    [string]$GameBin = "C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Singularity\Binaries",
    [string]$LocalRoot = "C:\Users\Trilex\vr-mods\SingularityVR-assets-local"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$here = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
$root = Resolve-Path (Join-Path $here "..\..")
$mh   = Join-Path $root "third_party\minhook"
if (-not (Test-Path $mh)) { throw "MinHook not found: $mh" }

$vswhere = "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe"
$vsPath  = & $vswhere -latest -products * -requires Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 -property installationPath
$vcvars  = Join-Path $vsPath "VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvarsall.bat"

Push-Location $here
try {
    $mhSrc = @(
        "`"$mh\src\buffer.c`"",
        "`"$mh\src\hook.c`"",
        "`"$mh\src\trampoline.c`"",
        "`"$mh\src\hde\hde32.c`""
    ) -join " "

    $cmd = "`"$vcvars`" x86 && cl /nologo /LD /EHsc /W3 /MD /std:c++17 " +
           "/I`"$mh\include`" " +
           "/Fe:dinput8.dll texture_injector.cpp $mhSrc " +
           "/link /DEF:dinput8.def user32.lib"
    cmd /c $cmd
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "build failed (exit $LASTEXITCODE)" }
    Write-Host "Built: $here\dinput8.dll"

    if ($Install) {
        if (-not (Test-Path $GameBin)) { throw "game Binaries not found: $GameBin" }

        $texDst = Join-Path $GameBin "texture-override"
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $texDst | Out-Null
        # clear old variant files so only the chosen one is present
        Get-ChildItem $texDst -Filter *.dds -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Remove-Item -Force

        # Every upscaled candidate for the chosen variant is deployed as <name>.dds,
        # which is exactly the filename the injector looks up per target.
        $suffix = if ($Variant -eq "B") { "__B_ibp" } else { "__A_lanczos" }
        $up = Join-Path $LocalRoot "textures\upscaled"
        if (-not (Test-Path $up)) { throw "upscaled dir missing: $up (run the pipeline 'upscale' step first)" }
        $strip = "$suffix.dds"
        $count = 0
        Get-ChildItem $up -Filter "*$suffix.dds" | ForEach-Object {
            $base = $_.Name.Substring(0, $_.Name.Length - $strip.Length)
            Copy-Item $_.FullName (Join-Path $texDst "$base.dds") -Force
            $count++
        }
        if ($count -eq 0) { throw "no '$suffix' candidates found in $up" }

# `asset-tools/texture-injector` �?" standalone first-person texture override (research)

A small, self-contained **32-bit `dinput8.dll` proxy** that substitutes
pre-upscaled DDS files for specific first-person textures at runtime.

It is **not** the VR mod and does **not** touch `d3d9.cpp`, the production
worktree, the game packages, `coalesced.tfc`, or the executable. It co-exists
with the VR `d3d9.dll` because it is injected through a different import
(`DINPUT8!DirectInput8Create`, which the EXE statically imports and for which no
`dinput8.dll` ships in `Binaries`).

Status: **verified working.** A game launch produced
`SUBSTITUTE inview_glove_n (1024x1024 -> 2048x2048)` and
`SUBSTITUTE inview_glove_d (1024x1024 -> 2048x2048)` with hashes matching the
extracted originals exactly.

## How it works

1. `dinput8.dll` loads at process start (static import) and forwards
   `DirectInput8Create` to a local copy of the real DLL, `dinput8_orig.dll`.
2. A worker thread hooks `Direct3DCreate9` / `Direct3DCreate9Ex` in the loaded
   `d3d9.dll`, then `IDirect3D9::CreateDevice` (vtable 16), then
   `IDirect3DDevice9::SetTexture` (vtable 65) �?" MinHook, chaining on top of the
   VR mod's own hooks.
3. On each `SetTexture`, for a texture that is 1024�-1024 DXT1 (i.e. a candidate),
   it locks mip 0 read-only and computes an **FNV-1a 64 hash of the compact DXT
   bytes**. If the hash equals a target's known original hash, it creates a
   2048�-2048 replacement texture from the configured DDS and binds that instead.
   Classification is cached per texture pointer.

4. Screen-Space Effects Corrupting Depth

If the game uses any screen-space shadows or early forms of Ambient Occlusion (SSAO), they will completely break in VR.
• The Issue: Screen-space effects look at the 2D depth buffer of a single flat screen. In VR, they stretch across the lenses because they don't understand the horizontal stereo offset (IPD).
• The Fix: Disable screen-space shadows/AO entirely in the engine config (bAllowAmbientOcclusion=False) to see if the glitch disappears. If it does, you'll need to rewrite the shader to utilize stereo-correct texture coordinates.

• Are you building this using an injection framework (like UEVR modified for UE3, or VorpX style hooks) or do you have source code access?
